sections.title: A) MODAL VERBS: POSSIBILITY · PROBABILITY · CERTAINTY

blocks.heading: La clave: la FORMA cambia según el MOMENTO del que hablas
blocks.rule: Presente / futuro → modal + inf (sin to). Ahora mismo (en progreso) → modal + be + V-ing. Pasado → modal + have + participio. Pasado en progreso → modal + have been + V-ing.
examples: She may be tired.
She may be having a shower.
Peter may have bought a new car.
Lois may have been having a shower when you arrived.

blocks.heading: POSSIBILITY: may / might / could
blocks.rule: Presente / futuro: may / might / could + inf. Negativa: may / might + not + inf ("puede que no"). ¡Ojo! could not / can't NO es posibilidad negativa: significa que es imposible.
examples: She may be tired.
She may not be at the library.
It could rain later.
blocks.tip: She might not be at home (= quizá no esté). She can't be at home (= es imposible que esté).

blocks.heading: CAN vs MAY / COULD para posibilidad
blocks.rule: Can → posibilidad GENERAL (algo que suele ocurrir), no un caso concreto. Para una ocasión concreta o el futuro → may / might / could (nunca can). Pasado incierto → could have (nunca can have).
examples: It can rain heavily in this region in autumn. (en general)
It might rain this evening. (esta tarde concreta)
I think it could rain later. (✗ can rain)
She could have gone to the supermarket. (✗ can have gone)

blocks.heading: POSSIBILITY: ahora mismo y en el pasado
blocks.rule: At the moment: may / might / could + be + V-ing. Pasado: may / might / could + have + participio. Pasado continuo: may / might + have been + V-ing.
examples: She may be having a shower.
Peter may have bought a new car.
Lois may have been having a shower when you arrived.

blocks.heading: PROBABILITY: may / might / could + WELL
blocks.rule: Well hace que sea MUY probable. Futuro: may / might / could + well + inf (o + be + V-ing). Pasado: may / might / could + well + have + participio.
examples: It may well rain tomorrow.
They may well be waiting for us.
He may well have won the competition.

blocks.heading: Extra (Complete Advanced): could easily · conceivably · just might · every possibility
blocks.rule: May / might / could + easily = posibilidad fuerte. May / might / could + possibly / conceivably, o just might = posibilidad REMOTA. There's (a / some / a slight / every / a good / strong / real) possibility / chance + that + oración o of + -ing. Is there any chance of + -ing? It's (just / quite / entirely) possible that...
examples: I'd better write it down, otherwise I could easily forget.
My boss could conceivably change her mind.
I just might have time to finish the report.
There's every possibility that the business will succeed.
Is there any chance of seeing you this weekend?

blocks.heading: PROBABILITY: be likely / unlikely to + inf
blocks.rule: Adjetivo + to inf. Funciona en cualquier tiempo cambiando el verbo be. También It is likely that + oración.
examples: It is likely to rain tomorrow.
He was unlikely to win the lottery.
It is likely that she will call.

blocks.heading: PROBABILITY: There is a little / slight / some / strong likelihood ...
blocks.rule: + of + V-ing (o of + objeto + V-ing) · + that + oración.
examples: There is a strong likelihood of it raining tomorrow.
There is a slight likelihood of him passing the exam.
There is a strong likelihood that it will rain tomorrow.
blocks.tip: Con of + V-ing pon el sujeto delante del verbo si no es obvio: of IT raining, of HIM passing (✗ of raining).

blocks.heading: CERTAINTY: futuro → be BOUND to + inf
blocks.rule: Para el futuro no hay verbo modal de certeza: usamos to be + bound + to inf (= es seguro que...).
examples: If you don't study, you are bound to fail the test.

blocks.heading: CERTAINTY: presente y pasado → must / can't / couldn't
blocks.rule: Presente: must + inf (+, estoy seguro de que sí) · can't / couldn't + inf (−, estoy seguro de que no). Pasado: must + have + participio · can't / couldn't + have + participio.
examples: You must be exhausted after the trip.
That can't be John — he's in Australia.
The lights are off; they must have gone to bed.
He can't have stolen the money; he was with me.
blocks.tip: El negativo de must (deducción) es can't, NUNCA mustn't. ✗ He mustn't have stolen it.

blocks.heading: SHOULD + inf: mucha probabilidad (expectativa)
blocks.rule: Reduce la certeza: algo es muy probable o lo esperamos, pero no es seguro.
examples: Real Madrid should win the league.
The parcel should arrive by Friday.

blocks.heading: Tabla resumen: grado de certeza × momento
blocks.rule: Lee la fila (cuánto de seguro estás) y la columna (cuándo).

sections.title: B) MODAL VERBS: OBLIGATION · PROHIBITION · ABILITY · PERMISSION · ADVICE · NECESSITY

blocks.heading: OBLIGATION: must / have to
blocks.rule: Must → obligación fuerte: leyes, normas escritas (y la que se impone el propio hablante). Have to → obligación externa, alguien te lo ordena. Must no tiene pasado ni futuro: usamos had to / will have to.
examples: You must wear a seatbelt.
I have to finish this report — my boss wants it today.
I had to work late yesterday.
You will have to wait.

blocks.heading: MUST vs HAVE TO: matiz del libro
blocks.rule: I have to finish this report = otra persona lo exige. I must finish this report = YO siento que es esencial. Must también da consejo fuerte: You must see this film!
examples: He has to go to the police station. (la policía se lo ha ordenado)
He must go to the police station. (yo creo que es esencial que vaya)

blocks.heading: Semi-modal: MAKE + alguien + inf (sin to)
blocks.rule: Obligar a alguien. En pasiva el TO vuelve: be made + to inf.
examples: My parents made me do the dishes.
I was made to wait outside.

blocks.heading: PROHIBITION vs LACK OF OBLIGATION
blocks.rule: Mustn't → prohibición (por ley / normas). En pasado / futuro: wasn't allowed to / won't be allowed to. Don't have to → falta de obligación: no es necesario, pero puedes.
examples: You mustn't smoke in hospitals.
We weren't allowed to use our phones.
You don't have to come if you don't want to.
blocks.tip: Mustn't ≠ don't have to. You mustn't go = está prohibido. You don't have to go = no es obligatorio.

blocks.heading: ABILITY: can / could / be able to / be capable of
blocks.rule: Can → habilidad general en presente. Could → habilidad general en el pasado. Be able to + inf / be capable of + V-ing → todos los tiempos, y para un logro concreto (esfuerzo para conseguir una meta). Negativas: unable / incapable.
examples: I can speak English.
I could run fast when I was a child.
As I trained every day, I was able to run the marathon.
He is incapable of telling a lie.
blocks.tip: Logro concreto en el pasado → was able to / managed to, no could: ✗ I could pass the exam yesterday. ✓ I was able to pass it. (Negativo sí: I couldn't pass it.)

blocks.heading: Semi-modal: MANAGE to + inf / SUCCEED in + V-ing
blocks.rule: Conseguir algo con dificultad.
examples: As I trained every day, I managed to compete.
She succeeded in passing the exam at the third attempt.

blocks.heading: COULD + HAVE + participio → habilidad que no se usó
blocks.rule: Podrías haberlo hecho, pero no lo hiciste. También para quejarse: You could have told me!
examples: I could have passed the test, but I wasn't fast enough.
You could have called me!

blocks.heading: PERMISSION: can / could / may · let · allow · permit
blocks.rule: Can / could / may → pedir permiso (may es el más formal). Can't / couldn't → falta de permiso. Let + alguien + inf (sin to). Allow / permit + alguien + to inf. Pasiva: be allowed / permitted to + inf (let no tiene pasiva).
examples: May I come in?
You can't park here.
My parents let me go out.
They don't allow us to use phones.
We weren't allowed to leave.

blocks.heading: ADVICE: should / ought to / must / had better
blocks.rule: Should / ought to + inf → consejo general (presente / futuro). Negativa: shouldn't / ought not to. Pasado (crítica): should / ought to + have + participio. Must → consejo fuerte o moral. Had better + inf (sin to) → consejo; si no, habrá una consecuencia negativa. Negativa: had better not.
examples: You should / ought to see a doctor.
You should have studied a lot more.
You must see that film — it's brilliant!
It's raining a lot; you'd better take an umbrella.
You'd better not be late.

blocks.heading: NECESSITY: need to · don't need to · needn't
blocks.rule: Presente: need to (+) · don't need to / needn't + inf (−). Pasado: didn't need to → no era necesario y NO lo hice. Needn't + have + participio → lo hice, pero no era necesario.
examples: You needn't come tomorrow.
I didn't need to take a taxi, so I walked.
I needn't have taken a taxi — the station was just around the corner.

blocks.heading: SHOWING ANNOYANCE: may / might / could + as well / at least
blocks.rule: May / might / could + as well + inf → da igual / ya que estamos (no hay nada mejor). Might / could + at least + inf → queja: "podrías al menos...". Pasado: could / might + (at least) + have + participio.
examples: There's nothing on TV; we might as well go to bed.
You could at least say thank you!
You might at least have called me!

blocks.heading: ZERO CONDITIONAL: If / When + present simple, present simple
blocks.rule: Verdades universales y hechos que siempre se cumplen (también past – past para hábitos pasados).
examples: If you heat water, it boils.
When you mix blue and yellow, you get green.

blocks.heading: 1st CONDITIONAL: If / When + present simple, will / may / can / could / should / must / be going to + inf
blocks.rule: Situación real que puede pasar o no en el futuro.
examples: If you study more, you will pass the test.
If it rains tomorrow, we may cancel the picnic.

blocks.heading: 1st CONDITIONAL más improbable: happen to / should
blocks.rule: If + sujeto + happen to / should / should happen to + inf → hace que el suceso sea MENOS probable (= si por casualidad). Inversión (formal): Should + sujeto + inf, ...
examples: If you happen to take the bus, you will arrive on time.
If you should see Anna, tell her I called.
Should you apply for the job, you will be hired.

blocks.heading: 2nd CONDITIONAL: If + past simple, would / could / might + inf
blocks.rule: Situaciones imaginarias o poco probables en el presente / futuro. Con be usamos SIEMPRE were (para todas las personas). If I were you → dar un consejo.
examples: If I had more money, I would travel the world.
If I were you, I would apologise.

blocks.heading: 2nd CONDITIONAL más improbable: were to + inf
blocks.rule: If + sujeto + were to + inf, would / could / might + inf. Inversión: Were + sujeto + to + inf, ...
examples: If I were to have more free time, I would go to the park.
Were I to win the election, I would reduce the fees.

blocks.heading: 3rd CONDITIONAL: If + past perfect, would / could / might + have + participio
blocks.rule: Situación pasada que no ocurrió: arrepentimientos y críticas sobre el pasado. Inversión: Had + sujeto + participio, ...
examples: If I had studied more, I would have passed the exam.
Had I studied more, I would have passed the exam.
blocks.tip: En la inversión, la negativa es Had + sujeto + not: Had I not studied... (✗ Hadn't I studied).

blocks.heading: MIXED CONDITIONALS
blocks.rule: 3rd + 2nd → If + past perfect, would / could / might + inf: situación PASADA que afecta al PRESENTE. 2nd + 3rd → If + past simple, would / could / might + have + participio: situación GENERAL (siempre es así) que afecta al PASADO.
examples: If I had eaten breakfast, I wouldn't be hungry now.
If I had studied more, I would have a better job now.
If I were taller, I could have become a pilot.
If he spoke English, he would have got the job.

blocks.heading: Otros usos de los condicionales (Complete Advanced)
blocks.rule: Formas continuas también valen en las dos partes. If you would + inf → crítica o petición fuerte. I'd appreciate it / I'd be grateful if you would / could → petición formal. Otherwise + would / could → idea condicional sin if. Alternativas a if: as soon as, in case, in the event that, assuming (that), given that, supposing.
examples: If I was driving, we'd be arriving by now.
If it hadn't been snowing, we wouldn't have got lost.
If you'd stop making so much noise, we'd all be able to enjoy the film.
I'd appreciate it if you could hand in the report by Thursday.
Supposing you lost your job, what would you do?

blocks.heading: Tabla resumen de condicionales
blocks.rule: Mira el tiempo de cada parte.

sections.title: D) ALTERNATIVES TO IF · WISH / IF ONLY

blocks.heading: Provided (that) / Providing / As long as / On condition that
blocks.rule: Condición estricta: "siempre y cuando". Van con present simple aunque hablen del futuro.
examples: You can borrow my car as long as you drive carefully.
They lent us the money on condition that we paid it back.

blocks.heading: Unless = if not (a menos que)
blocks.rule: Unless ya es negativo, así que el verbo va en afirmativo.
examples: We'll miss the train unless we leave now. (= if we don't leave now)

blocks.heading: Otherwise (de lo contrario) · Even if (incluso si)
blocks.rule: Otherwise va después de una orden o afirmación. Even if → el resultado no cambia aunque se cumpla la condición.
examples: Hurry up, otherwise we'll be late.
I wouldn't go even if they paid me.

blocks.heading: But for / Were it not for / Had it not been for (si no fuera por)
blocks.rule: But for + sustantivo (2nd o 3rd). Were it not for + sustantivo → 2nd conditional (presente). Had it not been for + sustantivo → 3rd conditional (pasado).
examples: But for your help, I would have failed the exam.
Were it not for the rain, we would go out.
Had it not been for the rain, we would have gone out.

blocks.heading: WISH / IF ONLY + past simple
blocks.rule: Queremos cambiar una situación o estado PRESENTE. Con be → were (también was en inglés informal).
examples: I wish I had more money.
If only I lived near the beach.
I wish I were taller.

blocks.heading: WISH + past continuous · wish en pasado
blocks.rule: Wish + past continuous → algo que está pasando / va a pasar y no te gusta. Si el verbo wish va en pasado (wished), el tiempo de detrás no cambia.
examples: I wish I didn't have to go to school today.
Jan wishes the wedding was taking place in the spring.
Peter wished he hadn't arranged to go out that evening.

blocks.heading: WISH / IF ONLY + past perfect
blocks.rule: Arrepentimiento sobre una situación PASADA.
examples: I wish I had studied more.
If only I hadn't told him the truth.

blocks.heading: WISH / IF ONLY + would
blocks.rule: Mostrar enfado o molestia por el comportamiento de OTRA persona (queremos que cambie). No se usa con I (✗ I wish I would).
examples: I wish my brother would not take my things.
I wish you would stop making that noise!

blocks.heading: WISH / IF ONLY + could
blocks.rule: Falta de habilidad o de posibilidad.
examples: I wish I could go to Javi's party.
I wish I could speak Chinese.

speaking.structure: They might have just [participle], which would explain why they look so [adjective].
speaking.example: They might have just received some good news, which would explain why they look so excited.
speaking.translation: Puede que acaben de [participio], lo que explicaría por qué parecen tan [adjetivo].

speaking.structure: Judging by [evidence], she must be [-ing / adjective]; she can't be enjoying it.
speaking.example: Judging by her expression, she must be feeling stressed; she can't be enjoying the experience.
speaking.translation: A juzgar por [evidencia], debe de estar [...]; no puede estar disfrutándolo.

speaking.structure: This option would work well, provided that [condition]; otherwise, [consequence].
speaking.example: This option would work well, provided that the council invests enough money; otherwise, it might fail.
speaking.translation: Esta opción funcionaría bien siempre y cuando [condición]; de lo contrario, [consecuencia].

speaking.structure: Were governments to [verb], I think there would be a significant improvement in [area].
speaking.example: Were governments to invest more in education, I think there would be a significant improvement in public health.
speaking.translation: Si los gobiernos [verbo], creo que habría una mejora significativa en [área].

speaking.structure: If I had [participle] when I was younger, I would be [adjective] now. I really wish I had.
speaking.example: If I had learnt to play an instrument when I was younger, I would be in a band now. I really wish I had.
speaking.translation: Si hubiera [participio] de pequeño, ahora sería [adjetivo]. Ojalá lo hubiera hecho.
